title: APU vs Taylor: tuition, size, location
summary: Azusa Pacific University (APU) versus Taylor University (Taylor). Also searched as Taylor vs APU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Taylor University and Azusa Pacific University are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes. Taylor University has an undergraduate enrollment of 2,025 students and is located in Upland, while Azusa Pacific University enrolls 2,759 undergraduates and is situated in Azusa. Tuition for in-state students at Taylor University is $40,490, compared to $44,458 at Azusa Pacific University. These differences in enrollment size, location, and tuition costs highlight some of the distinctions between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Taylor University and Azusa Pacific University differ in their tuition costs and student debt levels. Taylor University charges $40,490 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, whereas Azusa Pacific University has a higher tuition fee of $44,458 for both categories. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Taylor University is $20,500, while at Azusa Pacific University it is slightly higher at $23,219. These financial figures provide insight into the cost of attendance and potential debt burden for students at each institution.

In summary, Taylor University offers a lower tuition rate compared to Azusa Pacific University, with identical tuition fees for in-state and out-of-state students at each school. The median debt upon completion also tends to be lower at Taylor University, reflecting differences in the overall cost of education between the two universities.
